statusMessage: June Kessler is under arrest. Isaac's concealed recorder preserved her admissions, the empty sluice trap has been disarmed, and Celia's complete tape is secured under seal. The case ends in a pyrrhic resolution because Gideon Rusk was killed.

nora_mercer.detail: Finger burns have been cooled and dressed; smoke irritation remains, but she is mobile.

isaac_ward.detail: Right-palm and forearm burns have been cooled and dressed; painful but mobile.

sheriff_coroner_annex.name: Sheriff Hollis Cade
sheriff_coroner_annex.description: Hollowfield's broad-shouldered sheriff, visibly exhausted and protective of his jurisdiction.

sheriff_coroner_annex.name: Dr. Miriam Vale
sheriff_coroner_annex.description: The county medical examiner, precise and withdrawn behind round glasses.

woh_radio.name: Naomi Venn
woh_radio.description: Celia's producer, sharp-eyed and raw with barely controlled grief.

blackwater_pump_house.name: June Kessler
blackwater_pump_house.description: Hollowfield's former mayor, disarmed and in state custody at the Blackwater sluice works.

mercy_diner.name: Vera Bell
mercy_diner.description: The diner's steel-spined owner, watching the road through cat-eye glasses.

bell_farm.name: Dr. Amos Bell
bell_farm.description: A rangy farm veterinarian with windburned skin and an impatient manner.

saint_ledas_archive.name: Father Rowan Pike
saint_ledas_archive.description: A tired-eyed priest and guarded keeper of the church's labor archive.

northline_motel.name: Mae Orlov
northline_motel.description: The motel's glamorous, unsentimental owner, amused by other people's discomfort.

dredge_funeral_home.name: Silas Dredge
dredge_funeral_home.description: A gaunt, courtly mortician with the careful hands of an antiquarian.

items.name: Repaired Archive Reel 18-B
items.description: A seven-inch reel of quarter-inch audio tape found hidden beside WOHF's bulk eraser. Naomi Venn repaired its splices and stabilized one surviving fragment; most surrounding audio remains erased.

items.name: Torn Gold-Threaded Ceremonial Button
items.description: A heavy civic button bearing Hollowfield's wheat-sheaf seal, recovered beneath the west-basin railing. Cream wool and snapped gold thread remain caught through its shank.

items.name: Sealed West-Basin Water Sample
items.description: A properly labeled sample taken from the west aeration basin. Dr. Miriam Vale found its distinctive black diatoms and algaecide crystals to be microscopically consistent with material recovered from Celia Wren's lungs.

evidence.title: The Saint Orra Body
evidence.summary: Radio journalist Celia Wren, 38, was found suspended and mutilated in the abandoned Saint Orra Packing House at 8:18 p.m.

evidence.title: Unreturned Saint Orra Inspection Key
evidence.summary: The 1988 key register records inspection key 4 as issued to June Kessler during her plant-counsel years. Its return line is blank, and the south loading door shows no forced entry.

evidence.title: Surviving 1988 Red Rain Records
evidence.summary: Copies supplied by Mayor Kessler show that Sheriff Hollis Cade authorized removal of six bodies before state inspectors arrived. The packet also records that original dispatch sheets and six witness statements later disappeared, but does not establish why.

evidence.title: Celia's Unfinished Red Rain Broadcast
evidence.summary: Celia's locked script says her 10:00 p.m. broadcast would play the voice of a Hollowfield official who ordered an illegal 1988 bypass and then closed a flood gate while six workers remained below. The official's name is not written in the script.

evidence.title: Recovered Fragment from Reel 18-B
evidence.summary: A surviving section of Celia's damaged recording captures Mayor June Kessler saying, “I closed one gate. I saved the town.” Most surrounding context has been erased.

evidence.title: June's Civic Buick at 7:24 p.m.
evidence.summary: Vera Bell identifies Mayor June Kessler as the woman she saw driving Hollowfield's cream civic Buick and towing a town utility trailer toward Saint Orra Road. Mercy Diner's original register roll fixes the sighting at 7:24 p.m.

evidence.title: Blood and Hair Beneath the West-Basin Rail
evidence.summary: The west-basin railing was scrubbed very recently, but a shielded bolt retained blood and forcibly torn strands of dark, wavy hair. Dr. Miriam Vale's comparison identifies both as consistent with Celia Wren; formal DNA confirmation remains pending.

evidence.title: Blackwater Material in Celia's Lungs
evidence.summary: Celia's deep-lung fluid contains intact black diatoms and algaecide crystals microscopically consistent with Isaac's sealed sample from Blackwater's west aeration basin. Their deep placement shows she inhaled the water while alive.

evidence.title: Celia Was Sedated with Xylazine
evidence.summary: Dr. Miriam Vale found a disabling concentration of veterinary xylazine in Celia's blood. It was administered shortly before the drowning and would have left her conscious but weak and poorly coordinated.

evidence.title: Missing Xylazine Vial — Batch XB-441
evidence.summary: Bell Farm's signed 3:55 p.m. count records four sealed xylazine vials from batch XB-441. Only three remain, and the treatment log records no later use or disposal of the missing vial.

evidence.title: Burned Carbon Copy of the 1988 Emergency Minutes
evidence.summary: A partially burned carbon copy preserves the original Red Rain emergency entry ordering the illegal bypass and naming then-plant counsel June Kessler in the decision to close Gate Three while six workers remained below. The surviving official version replaces that passage with 'unforeseeable mechanical failure'; handwritten alteration marks carry Kessler's initials.

evidence.title: Cade Admits the Red Rain Cover-Up
evidence.summary: Sheriff Hollis Cade admits that, on June Kessler's orders, he removed the six workers' bodies before state inspection and falsified dispatch times and incident records. He says June knew the men remained below when she ordered Gate Three closed.

evidence.title: June Admits the Blackwater Struggle
evidence.summary: At Blackwater Pump House, June Kessler admits that she and Celia had an intimate relationship, that Celia intended to use private material in her broadcast, and that Celia scratched her during a physical struggle beside the west basin. June characterizes the death as an accident and denies deliberate murder.

evidence.title: June Confesses to Drugging and Drowning Celia
evidence.summary: Isaac's concealed recorder preserves June admitting that she stole the veterinary sedative, put it in Celia's coffee, and deliberately held Celia beneath the west-basin water until she stopped struggling.

evidence.title: June Confesses to Staging Celia at Saint Orra
evidence.summary: Isaac's concealed recorder preserves June admitting that she transported Celia's body to Saint Orra in the civic utility trailer, inflicted the bolt wound and mutilations after death, and copied the Hush Woman tableau to disguise the drowning as ritual violence. She acknowledges that the throat, abdomen, and wax-sealed ears became a personal punishment for Celia's methods.
